content:
customer_acme_ops: Hey team — our Console shows region 'eu-west' for app-redwood-prod, but the request logs/trace show served_region=us-central. Users in EU seeing an extra ~220ms RTT and increased egress cost. Can you help? Example req id: r-3f9c8a2b

maria_support: Sorry about the trouble. Can you paste a full request with headers (X-Request-ID) and timestamp? Also which API host are you hitting (api.redwood.ai or eu.api.redwood.ai)?

customer_acme_ops: We're hitting api.redwood.ai (no region subdomain). Sample curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-3f9c8a2b" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-model-v2","input":"test"}'
```
Timestamp: 2025-07-12T14:22:18Z

jon_custsuccess: tagging @lee_eng_oncall and @tara_runtime. We have SLA customer, pinging for priority.

lee_eng_oncall: looping in eng. Looking at traces for r-3f9c8a2b... saw it routed to us-central pool at 14:22:18. Routing policy: prefer eu-west -> fallback global. eu-west pool reported transient capacity drop at 14:22:17.

telemetry_bot: [alert] pool-eu-west capacity: 14:21:58 -> 14:22:20 transient-unavailable (count=3), avg-queue-latency=310ms

tara_runtime: kernel logs show serving_host=us-central-02, model shard loaded there. Console UI region badge is sourced from the customer's configured "preferred_region" field (eu-west) not from the actual serving_region. That's misleading.

maria_support: So Console is showing configured region, not runtime served region. Customer impact: UI misleads and billing/latency expectations broken. Suggest immediate mitigation?

tara_runtime: Short term: add 'served_region' to request-level logs and surface it in Console Live Requests. Medium term: change Console badge to 'configured (served)' or show both.

lee_eng_oncall: For immediate customer fix we can force-route their tenant to eu-west if capacity recovered; but that may queue requests. Alternative: show served_region and let customer choose.

customer_acme_ops: We prefer lower latency. Can you force-route back if capacity is ok? Also can you confirm where their billing was attributed?

jon_custsuccess: I'll open a billing ticket. For now @tara_runtime can you check whether requests that served from us-central were billed at us-central egress rates? We need to know immediate cost exposure.

tara_runtime: Checking... logs indicate egress tags=us-central for those requests, so billing likely shows us-central. I'll attach trace snippets.

maria_support: Repro steps for internal: 1) Hit api.redwood.ai without region subdomain from EU client. 2) Simulate eu-west transient pool OOM/scale-down. 3) Observe fallback routing to global US pool and Console badge unchanged. 4) Validate served_region shows us-central in logs.

lee_eng_oncall: Action items:
- tara_runtime: push quick telemetry change to add served_region to request metadata (hotfix) :eyes:
- eng-platform: review fallback policy to prefer region if capacity available within Xs
- support: notify customer with workaround

tara_runtime: I'll ship a small telemetry patch to prod toggled behind a feature flag. ETA 2h.

deploy-bot: Started deploy of feature/telemetry-add-served-region to prod at 14:41 UTC

maria_support: Thanks. @customer_acme_ops we'll update once the flag is live and we've confirmed served_region in Console Live Requests. Sorry for the confusion :pray:

customer_acme_ops: Appreciate the fast response. Please confirm when the served_region shows up so we can verify latency improvements.

lee_eng_oncall: Escalating a product ticket to make Console display actual served_region alongside configured preference. Filing now.

jon_custsuccess: billing ticket opened (#BILL-1247). I'll follow up with cost delta once we have raw egress numbers.

maria_support: Marking this as escalated -> eng-runtime + product. Will close thread once customer confirms fix.

customer_acme_ops: Ok, standing by. :thumbsup:
